newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan detains Japanese fishing vessel, 11 crew.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan detains Japanese fishing vessel, 11 crew.

text.p: Taiwanese prosecutors and marine police on Thursday night detained 11 crew on a Japanese fishing vessel on charges of penetrating the island's territorial waters, a government official said.

Marine police led by prosecutors chased three Japanese fishing boats off the southern county of Pingtung but two escaped, Shieh Dah-wen, fisheries department head of the cabinet's Council of Agriculture, told Reuters on Friday.
"Apparently, the Japanese vessel knew they had penetrated our 12-nautical-mile territorial waters," Shieh said by telephone.
The nine Japanese and two Indonesians on the vessel had been detained and were being questioned, he said.
Under Taiwan's fishery law, the vessel owner could be fined up to Taiwan $300,000 (US$11,000) and its harvests and fishing tools -- excluding the vessel -- could be confiscated, he said.
The Japanese vessel might also have violated the National Security Law, but that would be left to the judgement of prosecutors, Shieh said.
National Securities Law violatations can lead to three years in prison or fines up to T$90,000 (US$3,297) in Taiwan.
It was the first time Taiwan had detained a Japanese vessel since 1980, Taipei's United Daily News newspaper reported.

The incident was the most serious involving Taiwan and Japan since a major 1996 sovereignty dispute arising from rival claims to a chain of small uninhabited East China Sea isles known to Japan as the Senkakus and to Taiwan and China as the Diaoyus.
Tokyo's reassertion of sovereignty over the islands sparked months of anti-Japanese demonstrations in Chinese communities across Asia.
The protests reached a deadly climax in September when flotillas carrying Hong Kong and Taiwan activists staged numerous attempts to land and plant flags on the Japanese-held islands.
A prominent Hong Kong activist drowned in one such protest.
Beijing, Taipei and Tokyo all claim sovereignty over the isles west of Japan's Okinawa island and northeast of Taiwan and east of China's southeastern Fujian coast.
Tokyo's claim dates to 1895, when Japan defeated China and seized Taiwan and other territories. China has claimed sovereignty over the islands for centuries.
Taiwan has no diplomatic ties with Japan, which recognises only Beijing's Communist government.
